slots.practicalActivity: In your Trailhead Playground, open Setup > Object Manager and click through 5 standard objects (Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case), noting for each the Label, API Name, and whether it is standard or custom.
slots.deliverable: A written list of the 5 objects with their API names and standard/custom status.

slots.practicalActivity: Create one new record each for Account, Contact, Lead, and Opportunity in your Trailhead Playground (a fictional small business), navigating between them via global search and the Related tab.
slots.deliverable: 4 newly created records (1 Account, 1 Contact, 1 Lead, 1 Opportunity) in your org, with a note on how they relate to each other.

slots.practicalActivity: Create an Account for a fictional company and add 2 Contacts related to it. Confirm both appear automatically on the Account's Related tab, then edit one Contact's Account field to move it to a different Account and watch the related list update.
slots.deliverable: One Account with 2 Contacts attached (one later moved to a different Account), plus a one-sentence note on what changed on the Related list.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Lead, convert it with the Convert Lead action into an Account/Contact/Opportunity, then create a Case against the resulting Account describing a fictional support issue.
slots.deliverable: A converted Lead (now an Account, Contact, and Opportunity) plus one Case linked to that Account.

lessons.title: Products, Price Books and Quotes Overview

slots.practicalActivity: Create one Product, add it to the Standard Price Book with a List Price, then add that Product to your Chapter 1 Opportunity as an Opportunity Product (line item).
slots.deliverable: One Product priced in the Standard Price Book and attached to an Opportunity as a line item.

slots.practicalActivity: Log a Task and schedule an Event against your test Contact or Opportunity, then check the record's Activity Timeline to confirm both appear with the correct dates.
slots.deliverable: One completed Task and one scheduled Event visible in the Activity Timeline of a record you created earlier this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: From Object Manager, create a custom object called Energy Audit with a Label and Plural Label, generate a tab for it, and create one record.
slots.deliverable: A new custom object (API name ending in __c) with a tab and one saved record.

slots.practicalActivity: Open your custom Energy Audit object in Object Manager and tour every sub-tab (Fields & Relationships, Page Layouts, Lightning Record Pages, Buttons/Links/Actions, Record Types), noting what each currently contains.
slots.deliverable: A short written tour log naming what you found under each of the 5 sub-tabs for your custom object.

slots.practicalActivity: Without referring back to the lessons, build a second custom object from scratch for a different fictional business need (for example Course Enrollment or Service Appointment), give it a tab, and create 2 records that reference your existing Account or Contact data through a lookup.
slots.deliverable: A second custom object, independently built, with 2 records and a working lookup relationship to a standard object.

slots.practicalActivity: Using only the standard objects from this chapter (Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case) plus Activities, build one realistic customer-lifecycle chain for a single fictional customer: a Lead converted into an Account/Contact/Opportunity, a logged Case, and at least one Task and Event.
slots.deliverable: One end-to-end customer record chain (converted Lead, Case, Task, Event) all cross-linked to the same customer.

slots.practicalActivity: On your Energy Audit custom object, open Fields & Relationships and review the full list of field types offered under New, then create one custom Text field.
slots.deliverable: A new custom Text field on Energy Audit, plus a written list of at least 8 field types you saw offered.

lessons.title: Text, Number, Date and Checkbox Fields

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Number field (Panel Count), a Date field (Audit Date), and a Checkbox field (Passed Inspection) to Energy Audit, then fill them in on your existing records.
slots.deliverable: 3 new fields (Number, Date, Checkbox) added and populated on your Energy Audit records.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Picklist field Installation Type with at least 3 values and a Multi-Select Picklist Issues Found with at least 4 values, then set both on your Energy Audit records.
slots.deliverable: One Picklist and one Multi-Select Picklist field, both populated with real values on your records.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Formula field on Energy Audit that calculates something from your existing fields, such as a text formula combining Installation Type and Audit Date, or a checkbox formula flagging a high Panel Count.
slots.deliverable: One working Formula field whose output you verify against the source fields it reads from.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Master-Detail child object (Audit Finding) related to Energy Audit, add 2-3 child records with a Number field, then add a Roll-Up Summary field on Energy Audit that counts or sums that child field.
slots.deliverable: A working Roll-Up Summary field on Energy Audit whose count or sum matches the child Audit Finding records you created.

lessons.title: Field Properties: Required, Unique and External ID

slots.practicalActivity: Mark one Energy Audit field as Required and another as Unique, then try saving a record that violates each rule to see the validation error fire.
slots.deliverable: A written note of the two error messages Salesforce showed when you violated the Required and Unique constraints.

slots.practicalActivity: On the standard Account object, list 5 standard fields and create 1 new custom field (for example Preferred Contact Method), noting the API name pattern that tells the two apart.
slots.deliverable: A written side-by-side list of 5 standard fields and 1 custom field on Account with their API names.

slots.practicalActivity: Without instructions, design and build 4 new fields of 4 different types on your second custom object from Chapter 1 (not already used on it), including at least one Formula or Roll-Up Summary field, choosing field properties like required or unique yourself.
slots.deliverable: 4 newly built fields of varied types on your second custom object, with a written note on which properties you chose and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a full field dictionary for your Energy Audit object: one sentence per field stating its type and purpose, as if handing the object off to another administrator who has never seen it.
slots.deliverable: A one-page field dictionary (field name, type, purpose) for the Energy Audit custom object.

slots.practicalActivity: Confirm the Audit Finding to Energy Audit relationship you built is Master-Detail, then add a separate Lookup field from Energy Audit to Contact (the assigned inspector), and compare what happens when you delete a parent record under each relationship type.
slots.deliverable: One object with both a Master-Detail and a Lookup relationship, plus a written note on the delete behavior you observed for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a junction object (Audit Assignment) with two Master-Detail relationships, one to Energy Audit and one to Contact, so multiple inspectors can work multiple audits, and create 2-3 junction records.
slots.deliverable: A working junction object with two Master-Detail relationships and at least 2 records linking Contacts to Energy Audits many-to-many.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a small custom object representing an internal approval chain and add a Hierarchical relationship field to it, then write a paragraph explaining when you would reach for an External Lookup relationship instead.
slots.deliverable: A working Hierarchical relationship field on a custom object, plus a written paragraph on when External Lookup applies instead.

slots.practicalActivity: Create 2 Record Types on Energy Audit (Residential and Commercial), each with its own picklist value set for Installation Type, and save one record under each type.
slots.deliverable: 2 Record Types on Energy Audit with distinct picklist values, and one record saved under each.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a schema review of everything built so far in this course: list every object, its relationships, and flag at least one design decision you would reconsider, such as whether Audit Finding should really be its own object instead of a Record Type.
slots.deliverable: A written schema review (about half a page) covering every custom object built, its relationships, and one design decision you would reconsider.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Schema Builder, add Energy Audit, Audit Finding, Audit Assignment, Contact, and Account to the canvas, and arrange them to visually confirm your relationships match what you intended.
slots.deliverable: A Schema Builder canvas (screenshot or saved arrangement) showing your custom objects and their relationship lines to Account and Contact.

slots.practicalActivity: Open 3 of your records' URLs, copy the record ID from each, and verify the first 3 characters match the correct object's key prefix (look up Energy Audit's and Account's key prefixes in Object Manager's object details).
slots.deliverable: A written table of 3 record IDs with their object, key prefix, and confirmation that the prefix matches the object.

lessons.title: Designing a Simple Data Model From Requirements

slots.practicalActivity: Given the requirement "track rental properties, each with multiple Tenants, lease Agreements, and Maintenance Requests tied to a specific Agreement," design the object, field, and relationship model on paper first, then build at least the objects and relationships (not every field) in your Trailhead Playground.
slots.deliverable: A written data model plan for the rental-property scenario, plus the objects and relationships actually built in your org.

slots.practicalActivity: On your rental-property model, delete a parent Agreement record and confirm the correct child Maintenance Requests behave as expected for the relationship type you chose: cascade delete for Master-Detail, orphaned-but-intact for Lookup.
slots.deliverable: A written before/after note describing exactly what happened to child records when you deleted a parent, confirming your relationship-type choice was correct.

slots.practicalActivity: Using Schema Builder, add every object you built across the whole course (the Energy Audit family plus the rental-property model) onto one canvas and capture it as a one-page org data model reference.
slots.deliverable: One Schema Builder screenshot showing the complete set of custom objects and relationships built across the entire course.

slots.practicalActivity: Starting from a brand-new fictional requirement you invent yourself, independently design and build a complete data model with no lesson-by-lesson guidance: at least 2 custom objects, one Master-Detail and one Lookup relationship, 2 Record Types, 1 Formula field, and 1 Roll-Up Summary field.
slots.deliverable: A fully built, original custom data model in your Trailhead Playground meeting all 6 listed requirements, plus a one-paragraph write-up of the business scenario it represents.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can read and extend a real Salesforce org's data model: distinguishing standard from custom objects, choosing the right field and relationship types (including when to use Master-Detail vs. Lookup and how to build a many-to-many junction), and designing a correct, documented schema in Schema Builder directly from a business requirement.
